title: Response failure ontology and trace-hook integration for observability pipeline
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Goal: Create a unified 'response failure ontology' and wire new tracing hooks into our metrics/log pipelines so alerts and dashboards can quickly distinguish between timeout, overload, transport error (HTTP/gRPC), and model-level failures (OOM, invalid logits, invalid tokenization). This ticket scopes the schema, ingestion changes, dashboard panels, and a lightweight runbook mapping that oncall can use to prioritize mitigations.

Why: Current incident tooling surfaces opaque error counts and raw traces; responders spend minutes triaging whether the problem is networking, capacity, or model artifact. A clear surface of failure types + a direct trace linkage will reduce mean-time-to-detect and mean-time-to-restore for inference outages and SLO regressions.

Non-goals: This ticket does not change routing/fallback policies or autoscaler behavior. It provides telemetry and operator guidance; follow-up tickets will wire automated fallbacks and capacity controls.
acceptance_criteria: Failure ontology spec published in Confluence and approved by SRE/Runtime/Platform PMs
Tracing hooks added to runtime entry/exit points and to model decoder codepaths, emitting failure_type and failure_subtype tags
Metrics pipeline accepts failure_type dimension (via OTLP/span tags → metric labels) and counts by model, route, region
Log enrichment rule converts span failure tags into structured log fields for ELK/Kinesis ingestion
Dashboard: interactive panel showing failure distribution (timeouts, overload, model-error, transport-error) with drilldown to example traces and top contributing routes
Playbook mapping created with first-response actions for each failure_type and linked from the dashboard
End-to-end test that injects simulated failure spans and validates downstream metric and dashboard updates
implementation_notes: Failure ontology draft: primary types = timeout | overload | transport_error | model_error | config_error | auth_error
Subtypes: e.g., timeout -> client_read_timeout, server_kv_timeout; overload -> token_rate_limit, queue_length_exceeded; model_error -> OOM, decode_error, invalid_checkpoint

Trace hook placement: request entry, dispatch to runtime worker, kv-cache lookup, model forward, decode loop, response encode, response send. Use deterministic tag names: redwood.failure.type, redwood.failure.subtype, redwood.failure.code

Telemetry flow: OpenTelemetry spans -> tracing backend (Jaeger) -> span-processor extracts redwood.failure.* tags into Prometheus counters via otel-collector transform -> labels: model, route, region, deployment_id, failure_type
Backfill plan: best-effort script to scan recent traces for signature patterns (gRPC error codes, exception messages) and seed the dashboard for historical context
Privacy: no raw prompt contents should be emitted; span attributes must avoid user PII. See security checklist in links.
trades_and_decisions: Decision to prefer a small, composable ontology (6 top-level types) over long tail taxonomy to keep dashboards actionable
Trade: Adding failure tags at decode loop increases span cardinality; we only tag top-level spans and set subtype only on error paths to limit cardinality
Chosen ingestion path: otel-collector transforms to avoid touching runtime metric code; pros: minimal runtime deps; cons: relies on collector throughput
We will not include per-token failure markers initially to avoid high cardinality; evaluate in 2 sprints if needed for model-debugging runs
rollout_plan: Feature flag for trace enrichment (runtime-level) to enable in staging then canary to 10% of traffic
Collector transform deployed to staging pipeline with test dataset, then promoted to production with rate limiting
Dashboard created in Console staging space; after verification, published to all orgs internal dashboards and linked in oncall rota
Oncall training session and 1 pager distributed to SRE and runtime on-call teams
testing_plan: Unit tests for trace hook tag emission (mock spans)
Integration test that simulates gRPC error codes and verifies metric labels appear in Prometheus
E2E replay: synthetic traffic injected with injected model OOM exception to validate dashboard counts and example trace drilldown
Load test ensuring collector transform adds <15% CPU overhead at P95 ingest rates
comments: 2025-11-04 - Marcus Li: Initial spike complete. Hook placement verified in local runtime; emitting redwood.failure.type as span attribute. Observed 7% CPU increase with naive tagging — switching to error-path-only tagging.
2025-11-07 - Priya Shah (SRE): Reviewed ontology draft. Request to add 'auth_error' as top-level type (seen in customer incidents). Also asked for clear guidance on alert thresholds per type.
2025-11-09 - Elena Gomez (PM): Added requirement to include route and deployment_id labels on metrics for accurate cross-tenant alerting. Please ensure label cardinality budget is respected.

2025-11-11 - Marcus Li: Collector transform PR opened (see links). Using attribute-to-metric processor to generate redwood_failure_count{failure_type, model, route, region}. Need help validating makefile and CI stage from infra team.

2025-11-14 - Design review (Tom Nguyen): Dashboard mockups feedback: prefer stacked area for trend and a small multiples grid for top routes by failure share. Also suggested a 'suspected cause' quick filter (model vs infra).

2025-11-17 - Ava Patel: Running canary in staging with 10% traffic. One regression found: decode-timeout spans not propagated due to earlier try/catch swallowing. Marcus created follow-up ENG-99311 to fix exception propagation.
2025-11-18 - Marcus Li: Updated acceptance criteria to include end-to-end test and added backfill script. Moving to In Progress.
